# Bores that open into a tunnel

Original synthetic Apache-2.0 fixture for quiddity#307 (item 2). No customer geometry is used.
`bores_into_tunnel.step.gz` is generated by `tools/make_bore_into_tunnel_fixture.py`
(build123d 0.13.0; the command is in the script's docstring).

A 240 x 160 x 100 mm block has an R22 tunnel along x at z = 30. Six bores are drilled from the
top of R14 bosses whose faces are square to the bore, tilted 35 degrees off vertical:

- x = -90, d16: ends at the tunnel axis, wholly in air, no floor face.
- x = -10, d16: ends 0.8 mm before the tunnel wall on its axis, so the floor disc is only thin
  crescents of plane at its edges (the partly walled exit). Read as `flat` before the fix.
- x = -50, d16: as x = -90 but aimed 14 mm off the tunnel axis (recognised `unknown`).
- x = 30, d9: blind flat floor in material.
- x = 70, d9: vertical blind flat floor 2 mm above the tunnel crown.
- x = 110, d9: tilted blind flat floor 28 mm short of the tunnel axis.

The test is `tests/internal/bores_into_tunnel.rs`.

`blind_hole_floor_strip_between_passages.step.gz`, `blind_hole_floor_removed_under_axis.step.gz` and
`blind_hole_floor_under_small_cross_hole.step.gz`
come from the same script: a d20 blind hole (floor at z = 40) in an 80 x 80 x 60 block. The first has
two R8 passages along x at y = +-11, z = 40, leaving a strip of floor across the axis (`flat`). The
second has an R10 tunnel at y = 6, z = 36 that removes the floor under the axis (`through`).
The third has an R3 cross hole along x at y = 0, z = 38 under the floor and across the axis; 72% of
the floor remains (`flat`).
